overview: eThekwini Municipality provides essential services to residents of the greater Durban area including water, electricity, refuse removal, rates and taxes, housing, and infrastructure maintenance. It is the largest municipality in KwaZulu-Natal.

services.name: Rates and Taxes
services.description: Property rates are charged annually based on the municipal valuation of your property. All property owners must pay rates.

common_problems.problem: Bill is much higher than expected
common_problems.likely_cause: Municipal revaluation increased your property value, or estimated readings were used instead of actual meter readings
what_to_do: Check if the meter reading on your bill matches your actual meter
If estimated: submit your actual reading at an eThekwini customer care centre or online
If the property valuation is wrong: object during the next General Valuation period
You can object to your property valuation within the published objection period under the Municipal Property Rates Act 6 of 2004

common_problems.problem: Receiving bills for a property you no longer own
what_to_do: Contact eThekwini Revenue department with proof of sale (transfer deed)
The conveyancing attorney who handled the sale should have notified the municipality
If they didn't, you may need to lodge a formal complaint and provide the transfer documents

common_problems.problem: Account in arrears and threatening disconnection
what_to_do: Apply for an indigent subsidy if your household income is below R4,500 per month
Request a payment arrangement — eThekwini must offer this before disconnection
eThekwini may NOT disconnect water supply to residential properties for non-payment (Constitutional Court ruling: Mazibuko v City of Johannesburg)
They CAN restrict water flow but not cut it off completely

indigent_subsidy.what: Free basic services for qualifying households: 9kL of water, 50kWh of electricity, and free refuse removal per month
indigent_subsidy.eligibility: Combined household income below R4,500 per month
how_to_apply: Visit your nearest eThekwini customer care centre
Bring ID documents of all household members
Proof of income or sworn affidavit of unemployment

services.name: Water and Sanitation
services.description: eThekwini Water and Sanitation (EWS) provides water supply and sewerage services.

report_problems.burst_pipe: Call 080 131 3013 (24-hour emergency) or use the eThekwini Connect app
report_problems.no_water: Check if there is a planned outage on the eThekwini website first. If not planned, report via 080 131 3013
report_problems.sewage_overflow: Report immediately to 080 131 3013 — this is a health emergency
report_problems.water_quality: Report discoloured or foul-smelling water to 080 131 3013

your_rights: Section 27(1)(b) of the Constitution: everyone has the right of access to sufficient water
The Water Services Act 108 of 1997 guarantees basic water supply
eThekwini must provide at least 6,000 litres (6kL) of free water per household per month to registered indigent households

services.name: Electricity
services.description: eThekwini Electricity provides power to most areas in the metro. Some areas are supplied directly by Eskom.

prepaid_vs_conventional.prepaid: Buy tokens at retail outlets, banks, or the eThekwini website. Enter the 20-digit token on your meter.
prepaid_vs_conventional.conventional: Billed monthly based on meter readings. Pay at customer care centres, online, or via bank.

common_problems.what_to_do: Try Key Revision Number (KRN) change — contact eThekwini Electricity at 080 131 3111. Your meter may need a software update.

common_problems.problem: No electricity and neighbours have power
common_problems.what_to_do: Check your circuit breaker first. If it's tripped, reset it. If it keeps tripping, you likely have a wiring fault — call a registered electrician. If it's not tripped, call 080 131 3111.
Check the eThekwini or Eskom load shedding schedule for your area at loadshedding.eskom.co.za or the EskomSePush app

services.name: Housing
services.description: eThekwini Human Settlements provides subsidised housing (RDP houses) and manages the housing waiting list.
how_to_apply: Visit your nearest eThekwini housing office
You must be a South African citizen over 21
Combined household income must be below R3,500 per month
You must not own or have previously owned property
You will be placed on the National Housing Needs Register
Waiting periods are extremely long — 10-20+ years in some areas
common_problems: House allocated to the wrong person — report to the housing office with your registration number
RDP house has structural defects — report within 5 years to claim under the National Home Builders Registration Council (NHBRC) warranty

services.name: Refuse Removal and Waste Management
services.description: eThekwini DSW (Durban Solid Waste) handles refuse collection, recycling, and illegal dumping.
services.collection_schedule: Weekly collection on a fixed day for your area. Check the eThekwini website or call 080 131 3013 for your collection day.
services.missed_collection: Report via the eThekwini Connect app or call 080 131 3013
services.illegal_dumping: Report via the eThekwini Connect app or call 080 131 3013 — include photos and location if possible

escalation.step_1: Contact the eThekwini Customer Care Centre for your area
escalation.step_2: If unresolved, email the City Manager's office: citymanager@durban.gov.za
escalation.step_3: Contact your Ward Councillor — find yours at www.ethekwini.gov.za
escalation.step_4: Lodge a complaint with the KZN MEC for Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs
escalation.step_5: Lodge a complaint with the Public Protector: 0800 11 20 40
escalation.legislation: Municipal Systems Act 32 of 2000, Municipal Property Rates Act 6 of 2004, Water Services Act 108 of 1997

your_rights: Section 152 of the Constitution requires municipalities to provide services in a sustainable manner
The Municipal Systems Act requires municipalities to consult communities on service delivery changes
You have the right to access your municipal account and dispute any charges
You cannot be disconnected from water without due process
You have the right to a basic level of municipal services
You have the right to participate in your ward committee and raise service delivery issues
